McLaren: McLaren’s front wing now features a redesigned end‑plate that smooths the air hitting the car’s nose, giving the car a cleaner “flow” into the rest of the aerodynamics. That extra bite means more grip in the corners and a steadier feel on the straights, helping the drivers extract lap‑time right out of the gate this weekend. In short, the tweak should translate into quicker corner exits and better tyre temperatures when it counts most.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has added a set of tiny winglets along the centre of the rear wing. The extra surface gives the car a bit more bite in the rear, helping it stay stable through the high‑speed corners and under heavy braking. In practice, that extra grip should let the drivers push a little harder and keep the car balanced over the weekend’s layout.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull’s new front wing now has a reshaped junction between the wing’s main elements and the endplates, plus a bit more camber on the flaps. The tweaks smooth the airflow and give the team a broader range of front‑end balance, meaning they can dial in more grip and stability in the tight corners of this weekend’s circuit. In short, the car should feel more predictable and quicker through the twisty sections.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has given the car a tighter‑pack front end – a new front‑wing footplate, reshaped nose and extra dive‑plane vanes – to clean up the airflow and make the front more stable through the high‑speed corners. Under the car the floor and diffuser have been slimmed and re‑profiled, with new edge profiles and winglet angles that boost rear down‑force without adding drag. All of these tweaks should translate into better grip and more predictable handling this weekend, giving the Scuderia a stronger platform for qualifying and race‑pace battles.
Williams Racing: Williams has added new winglets to the rear‑wing fairing and extended the third‑element flap. The extra surfaces give the car a bit more rear‑end grip, which should make it more stable through fast corners and help the drivers get the most out of their tyres. In short, the tweak aims to boost cornering speed and consistency for this weekend’s track.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls have tweaked the front wing for this circuit, adding extra flap‑adjustment points so they can fine‑tune the balance and get more grip out of the corners. At the rear, the diffuser’s shape has been reshaped and tied more closely into the crash structure, smoothing the airflow and giving the car a stronger push down the straight. Together, these changes should make the RB feel more stable under braking and quicker out of the fast sections, giving the drivers a better shot at a solid weekend.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin did not submit any updates for this event.
Haas F1 Team: Haas has tweaked the rear‑impact structure on the car, stiffening it so the chassis can take the high‑speed bumps and cornering forces more cleanly. The result should be a more stable rear end, giving the drivers better grip and confidence when they’re pushing the brakes and accelerating out of turns. In short, the car will feel more planted this weekend, helping Haas extract a bit more speed without sacrificing reliability.

Cadillac: Cadillac has added a set of little vents on the top of the rear sidepod and a new fairing around the rear‑wing actuator. The vents help pull heat out of the car so the engine stays in its sweet spot, while the fairing smooths airflow to cut drag. Together they should keep the power unit cooler and the car quicker on the straights, giving Cadillac a better chance to fight for position this weekend.
